questions.question: What do the columns of a 2×2 matrix represent geometrically?
options: The new positions of the standard basis vectors î and ĵ after transformation
questions.explanation: Column 1 shows where î = [1,0] lands, Column 2 shows where ĵ = [0,1] lands. Every other vector follows as a linear combination of these transformed basis vectors.

questions.question: What happens if a matrix has determinant = 0?
options: The space is compressed to a lower dimension (information is destroyed)
questions.explanation: Determinant 0 means the transformation collapses space (e.g., squishes 2D down to a line or a point). The matrix is not invertible — you can't undo the transformation because information was lost.

questions.question: Why are eigenvalues of the Hessian matrix relevant to training NeRF?
options: They control the curvature of the loss landscape — wildly different eigenvalues cause optimization instability
They determine the number of layers
questions.explanation: When eigenvalues differ by orders of magnitude (e.g., 0.001 vs 1000), gradient descent oscillates in the high-curvature direction and barely moves in the low-curvature one. This is the condition number problem that Positional Encoding helps mitigate.
